title: Bringing Humanoids to LeRobot
gist: Hugging Face's LeRobot adds a humanoid stack for the Unitree G1 in which a fine-tuned π0.5 VLA predicts 64-D SONIC latent motion tokens and a small on-robot controller (42M params) decodes them into stable 29-DoF whole-body motion. The post also covers competing whole-body controllers (NVIDIA GR00T-WholeBodyControl, Amazon FAR Holosoma), low-cost open hardware (under-$20 glove, ~$2,500 biped), a growing pool of large humanoid datasets on the Hub, and planned ASIMOV support.

insights.claim: For biped humanoids, VLA inference is too slow to control balance dynamics directly, so LeRobot inserts a fast whole-body controller between the learned policy and the robot: the policy predicts compact motion tokens and the controller converts them into dynamically feasible joint targets.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Humanoid autonomy is converging on a two-tier stack (slow foundation-model planner + fast learned controller); value accrues to whoever owns the controller/token layer, not only the VLA.
insights.quote: VLA inference alone is too slow to control those dynamics directly.
insights.locator: Why humanoids need a different control stack

insights.claim: Decoupling the VLA from the whole-body controller lets the learned policy avoid rediscovering balance and whole-body coordination from a small task-specific dataset, lowering data requirements for new humanoid tasks.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Reusable pretrained motion controllers act as a data-efficiency multiplier, making per-task humanoid deployment cheaper.
insights.quote: Separating the VLA from the controller means that the learned policy does not have to rediscover balance and whole-body coordination from a relatively small task dataset.

insights.claim: SONIC is a 42-million-parameter autoencoder trained on more than 100 million motion frames from BONES-SEED retargeted to the Unitree G1; its small size lets it run on the robot itself, where low latency prevents executed trajectories from diverging from desired ones.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: On-device, small-model inference is a hard requirement for humanoid control, favoring edge compute over cloud inference for the low-level loop.
insights.locator: SONIC is a relatively small autoencoder

insights.claim: SONIC encodes heterogeneous motion sources (VR poses, reference joints, human motion, video-derived motion, learned-policy output) into a shared 64-D quantized motion token that its decoder combines with recent proprioceptive history to produce executable joint targets.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: A universal motion-token interface could let human video and teleop data become training signal for robots, widening the usable data supply.
insights.locator: In this architecture, different motion sources

insights.claim: The OpenHLM paper found that loco-manipulation performance on its benchmark largely saturates at around 40 demonstrations per task when training π0.5 to predict SONIC motion tokens on the Unitree G1.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: If tens of demos per task suffice, the marginal cost of teaching humanoids new tasks is low, accelerating commercial task coverage.
insights.quote: performance across its benchmark largely saturates at around 40 demonstrations per task.

themes.theme: G1 demo pipeline and training cost

insights.claim: A can pick-and-place humanoid policy was trained from roughly 100 episodes (about 71 minutes) of whole-body teleoperation at 50 fps with three 480x640 cameras, a 31-D state and a 66-D action (64 SONIC latent + 2 gripper), fine-tuning lerobot/pi05_base for 12,000 steps on 4 H100 GPUs.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Useful humanoid skills can be fine-tuned with about an hour of data and a single 4-GPU node, implying modest compute demand per skill versus pretraining.

insights.claim: LeRobot's Unitree G1 build adds OpenArm grippers via 3D-printed wrist adapters, a head-mounted egocentric camera and a back enclosure housing a CAN-FD adapter, with printable parts released openly and much of the design adapted from the Unfolding Robotics project.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Unitree G1 is becoming the de facto open research humanoid platform, strengthening Unitree's ecosystem position.

insights.claim: A LoRA-on-SONIC policy trained with PPO in mjlab using head-camera depth dodged 79.1% of resolved thrown balls in a three-seed simulation evaluation, versus 0% with blank depth and 97.4% for a privileged oracle with true ball state; the authors stress this is not a measured hardware success rate.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Reactive humanoid skills can be bolted onto a pretrained controller via cheap adapters, but sim-to-real gaps remain unquantified.
insights.quote: This is a simulation result, not a measured hardware success rate.

insights.claim: In the ball-dodging experiment, reward-only PPO failed to learn reliable dodging; an auxiliary objective forcing the visual percept (frozen Theia-Tiny plus a 16-frame temporal adapter producing a 128-D vector) to predict ball position and velocity was key to success.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Perception-heavy robot RL still depends on hand-designed auxiliary supervision, a sign the field is not yet purely end-to-end.
insights.quote: PPO with reward alone did not learn to dodge reliably.
insights.locator: The vision pathway uses a frozen Theia-Tiny

insights.claim: LeRobot supports multiple whole-body controllers for the Unitree G1, including NVIDIA GR00T-WholeBodyControl and Amazon FAR Holosoma alongside SONIC, and offers a space to compare them.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Big Tech (NVIDIA, Amazon) is competing to own the humanoid whole-body-control layer; Hugging Face positions itself as the neutral integration hub.

insights.claim: Hugging Face's stated goal for LeRobot humanoids is to connect all open-source humanoid tools, models and data so researchers and AIs spend time on robot learning rather than rebuilding the stack, with support for Menlo Research's open-source ASIMOV humanoid coming next.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Watch for LeRobot becoming the default open humanoid software layer, which commoditizes the stack and shifts differentiation to hardware and data.
insights.locator: Where humanoids in LeRobot go next

insights.claim: The open-source Homunculus teleoperation glove uses an ESP32-C3 board reading 16 SS49E Hall-effect sensors, costs under $20 in materials, and is integrated into LeRobot to drive the HOPE-Jr hand.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Dexterous-data capture hardware is collapsing in cost, lowering barriers to dexterous-manipulation data collection.

insights.claim: Open-source humanoid hardware prices cited: the LeRobot-integrated HOPE-Jr arm and hand cost about €500, and Virgile Batto's fully 3D-printed 12-DoF LeRobot Humanoid biped (RobStride CAN-FD actuators, Raspberry Pi 5) has a BOM of about $2,500.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Sub-$3k DIY bipeds put deflationary pressure on low-end humanoid research platforms and broaden the developer base.

insights.claim: The Homunculus exoskeleton measures operator arm joint motion directly rather than reconstructing it from a few tracked points, and was used to produce a public G1 dataset of 550 episodes and about 475k frames.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Direct joint-measuring teleop rigs may yield higher-fidelity demos than VR-only capture.

insights.claim: Public humanoid datasets on the Hugging Face Hub are reaching substantial scale: HIW-500 has 500+ hours and 23K episodes of Unitree G1 teleoperation across 12 real homes, OMG-Data has roughly 798K G1 motion episodes, BONES-SEED has 142K+ annotated human motions (~288 hours), and eidon-ai/tracker-pov has 1,274 hours of egocentric household video with IMU arm tracking.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: The humanoid data bottleneck is easing via open datasets concentrated on the Unitree G1, reinforcing it as the reference platform.

insights.claim: Approaches like EgoHumanoid combine robot demonstrations with robot-free egocentric human data from VR headsets and head-mounted cameras in a common training interface, pointing to human video as a scalable source of humanoid training data.
insights.speaker: Martino Russi
insights.so_what: Egocentric human-data capture (wearables, VR) could become a valuable input market for humanoid training.
